#!/usr/bin/env bash
# sync-to-codex.sh -- rebuild the Codex and agent-pool VIEWS from the canonical
# repo at ~/.claude/skills.
#
# CANONICAL: ~/.claude/skills   (git repo erash11/claude-skills, real dirs only)
# VIEWS:     ~/.agents/skills   (Pi, Cowork)
#            ~/.codex/skills    (Codex)
#
# Views are GENERATED from the complete canonical manifest - every directory
# holding a SKILL.md, plus declared support directories. Never author a skill
# in a view; it will be overwritten.
#
# On macOS a view entry is a symlink; on Windows the .ps1 twin copies instead.
# A written manifest records which view entries this script owns, so an audit
# can tell a generated entry from a third-party install it must not touch.
set -euo pipefail

SRC="$HOME/.claude/skills"
SUPPORT=(_shared)                 # no SKILL.md, but views need them
MODE="${SYNC_MODE:-link}"         # link | copy
DRY="${DRY_RUN:-0}"
MANIFEST_NAME=".generated-by-sync-to-codex"

# R8-01: OWNERSHIP IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A LIST.
#
#   a real directory in ~/.claude/skills  = Eric wrote it   -> ours to publish
#   a symlink in ~/.claude/skills          = installed by the
#                                            skills CLI or vendored
#                                                            -> never ours
#
# All 19 outward links here are third-party (14 recorded in
# ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json, 4 from the vendor-review package, plus
# persistent-localhost). No hard-coded name list is kept: it was 4 names
# yesterday, is 19 today, and changes on the next `npx skills add`.

# R2-01: publish EVERY canonical skill, not a hand-kept list of seven.
# A hard-coded SHARED array is why the pool drifted and why 8 canonical
# skills were missing from it entirely.
MANAGED=()
THIRD_PARTY=()
# R9-06: glob "$SRC"/* with NO trailing slash. "$SRC"/*/ matches only links
# that RESOLVE to directories, so a dangling third-party link was silently
# left out of the exclude list and the next `git add -A` would commit it.
for d in "$SRC"/*; do
  name="$(basename "$d")"
  case "$name" in .*) continue ;; esac
  # A symlink can NEVER enter MANAGED - dangling or not. That makes the
  # original R1 danger (delete-then-copy destroying a link target)
  # structurally impossible.
  if [ -L "$d" ]; then
    THIRD_PARTY+=("$name")
    [ -e "$d" ] || echo "WARN third-party link '$name' is dangling" >&2
    continue
  fi
  if [ -d "$d" ] && [ -f "$d/SKILL.md" ]; then
    MANAGED+=("$name")
  fi
done
for s in "${SUPPORT[@]}"; do
  if [ -d "$SRC/$s" ] && [ ! -L "$SRC/$s" ]; then
    MANAGED+=("$s")
  fi
done

if [ "${#MANAGED[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "FATAL no skills found under $SRC - refusing to wipe the views." >&2
  exit 2
fi

echo "canonical manifest: ${#MANAGED[@]} entries; third-party links: ${#THIRD_PARTY[@]}"

# The ONE guard worth keeping: a name we previously OWNED and published has
# become a symlink in canonical. That means someone inverted an owned skill
# by hand, and its real content now lives outside the repo. A link that is
# NOT in the old manifest is just a fresh `npx skills add` - normal, logged.
for dst_probe in "$HOME/.agents/skills" "$HOME/.codex/skills"; do
  [ -f "$dst_probe/$MANIFEST_NAME" ] || continue
  # ${arr[@]+...} form: macOS /bin/bash is 3.2, where expanding an EMPTY
  # array under `set -u` aborts with "unbound variable".
  for name in ${THIRD_PARTY[@]+"${THIRD_PARTY[@]}"}; do
    if grep -qxF -- "$name" "$dst_probe/$MANIFEST_NAME"; then
      echo "FATAL '$name' was an owned, published skill and is now a symlink in" >&2
      echo "      canonical. Its real content has moved outside the repo." >&2
      echo "      Restore it as a real directory before syncing. No changes made." >&2
      exit 2
    fi

done

# R8-02 + R9-02: keep git from ever seeing the current canonical links, so the
# daily backup's `git add -A` cannot commit an `npx skills add` link.
#
# Written to .git/info/exclude, NOT the tracked .gitignore. The set of links is
# per-machine, while .gitignore is shared through erash11/claude-skills: each
# machine's sync would rewrite the other's list, the backup would push it, and
# the Mac's links would stop being ignored - R3 again. info/exclude is never
# committed. Lines outside the marked block (e.g. /.claude/RESUME.md) are kept.
# The pre-commit hook from Task 3 is the backstop for a link installed after
# the last sync.
EXCL="$SRC/.git/info/exclude"
BEGIN="# BEGIN generated-by-sync-to-codex: third-party symlinks"
END="# END generated-by-sync-to-codex"
if [ "$DRY" = "0" ] && [ -d "$SRC/.git" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$SRC/.git/info"
  tmp="$(mktemp)"
  if [ -f "$EXCL" ]; then
    awk -v b="$BEGIN" -v e="$END" '
      $0==b {skip=1} !skip {print} $0==e {skip=0}' "$EXCL" > "$tmp"
  fi

    echo "$BEGIN"
    echo "# Rewritten on every sync. Per-machine. Do not edit by hand."
    echo "# No trailing slash: that matches directories only, and git does not"
    echo "# treat a symlink as a directory - the pattern would never match."
    for name in ${THIRD_PARTY[@]+"${THIRD_PARTY[@]}"}; do echo "/$name"; done
    echo "$END"

    cp "$tmp" "$EXCL"
    echo "updated $EXCL (${#THIRD_PARTY[@]} third-party links excluded)"
  fi
  rm -f "$tmp"
fi

# R3-02: the manifest is a writable file inside a view. Never hand any line
# of it to rm without proving it is a single plain basename. A line reading
# '../../.claude/skills' would otherwise delete the canonical repository on
# the next dev-sync. Separators, dot components and empties are all refused.
valid_entry() {
  case "$1" in
    ''|.|..)            return 1 ;;
    */*|*\\*)           return 1 ;;   # any path separator
    .*)                 return 1 ;;   # hidden, incl. the manifest itself
    *\**|*\?*|*\[*|*\]*) return 1 ;;  # R4-01: glob metacharacters
    -*)                 return 1 ;;   # cannot be mistaken for an option
  esac
  return 0
}

ARCHIVE_ROOT="$HOME/.agents/skills-archive/retired-$(date +%F)"

for dst in "$HOME/.agents/skills" "$HOME/.codex/skills"; do
  mkdir -p "$dst"
  KEEP_OWNED=()          # refused entries stay tracked (R5-01)
  # Retire entries this script generated before but no longer manages, so a
  # skill deleted from canonical also disappears from the views. Entries NOT
  # in the old manifest are third-party installs and are never touched.
  if [ -f "$dst/$MANIFEST_NAME" ]; then
    while IFS= read -r old; do
      if ! valid_entry "$old"; then
        [ -n "$old" ] && echo "REFUSE manifest entry '$old' is not a plain name - ignored" >&2
        continue
      fi
      # Literal, whole-line match. grep -x alone would treat the entry as a regex.
      if printf '%s\n' "${MANAGED[@]}" | grep -qxF -- "$old"; then
        continue
      fi
      # Prove containment: the resolved parent must be the view itself.
      parent="$(cd "$dst" 2>/dev/null && cd "$(dirname "./$old")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || {
        KEEP_OWNED+=("$old"); continue
      }
      if [ "$parent" != "$(cd "$dst" && pwd)" ]; then
        echo "REFUSE '$old' resolves outside $dst - ignored" >&2
        KEEP_OWNED+=("$old")
        continue
      fi
      echo "retire $old from $dst (no longer in canonical)"
      # R5-01: use -e OR -L. When a canonical skill is deleted upstream and
      # dev-sync pulls that deletion, the generated Mac symlink goes dangling
      # and -e alone is FALSE - the link would survive while its name was
      # dropped from the manifest, leaving permanent untracked view debris
      # that the audit could not see.
      if [ "$DRY" = "0" ] && { [ -e "$dst/$old" ] || [ -L "$dst/$old" ]; }; then
        # R4-02: archival must SUCCEED before removal, and each view gets its
        # own archive subdirectory. A shared path meant the second view's
        # (possibly different) copy was deleted without being preserved,
        # and a suppressed copy failure meant an unarchived delete.
        # Strip the leading dot: an archive under '.agents/' is a hidden
        # directory a human looking for their retired skill will not see.
        view_tag="$(basename "$(dirname "$dst")" | sed 's/^\.//')"   # agents | codex
        adir="$ARCHIVE_ROOT/$view_tag"
        mkdir -p "$adir" || { echo "FATAL cannot create $adir" >&2; exit 3; }
        if [ -e "$adir/$old" ] || [ -L "$adir/$old" ]; then
          echo "FATAL archive collision at $adir/$old - refusing to delete" >&2
          exit 3
        fi
        # -P copies a symlink AS a link, so a dangling one archives fine
        # without needing its target to exist.
        if ! cp -RP "$dst/$old" "$adir/$old"; then
          echo "FATAL archive of '$old' failed - refusing to delete" >&2
          exit 3
        fi
        if [ ! -e "$adir/$old" ] && [ ! -L "$adir/$old" ]; then
          echo "FATAL archive of '$old' not readable back - refusing to delete" >&2
          exit 3
        fi
        rm -rf "$dst/$old"
      fi
    done < "$dst/$MANIFEST_NAME"
  fi

  for s in "${MANAGED[@]}"; do
    if [ "$DRY" = "1" ]; then
      echo "would sync $s -> $dst ($MODE)"
      continue
    fi
    # Safe: $SRC/$s is proven real, so removing the view cannot touch it.
    rm -rf "${dst:?}/${s:?}"
    if [ "$MODE" = "link" ]; then
      ln -s "$SRC/$s" "$dst/$s"
    else
      cp -R "$SRC/$s" "$dst/$s"
    fi
  done

  if [ "$DRY" = "0" ]; then
    # R5-01: ownership is only released when retirement actually succeeded.
    # An entry we REFUSED stays in the manifest, so it remains tracked and
    # the next run (or the audit) still sees it, instead of becoming
    # untracked debris.
    if [ "${#KEEP_OWNED[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "${MANAGED[@]}" "${KEEP_OWNED[@]}" | sort -u > "$dst/$MANIFEST_NAME"

    else
      printf '%s\n' "${MANAGED[@]}" > "$dst/$MANIFEST_NAME"
    fi
    echo "synced ${#MANAGED[@]} entries -> $dst ($MODE); manifest written"
  fi
done

fi
exit 0

  }
}

foreach ($dst in @((Join-Path $HOME '.agents\skills'), (Join-Path $HOME '.codex\skills'))) {
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dst | Out-Null
  $manifestPath = Join-Path $dst $MANIFESTNAME
  $KEEP_OWNED   = @()   # R8-11: refused retirements stay tracked, as in bash

  # Retire entries no longer managed. R3-02: validate each line is a plain
  # name before it reaches Remove-Item, and archive before removing.
  if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $manifestPath) {
    # R4-01: EVERY manifest-derived filesystem call uses -LiteralPath, and
    # wildcard metacharacters are refused before any mutation. Without this a
    # manifest line of '*' passes a separator check and then expands inside
    # Remove-Item's wildcard-aware -Path, wiping third-party entries and the
    # Codex .system assets.
    foreach ($old in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $manifestPath)) {
      $old = $old.Trim()
      if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($old)) { continue }
      if ($old -match '[\\/]' -or $old -match '[\*\?\[\]]' -or
          $old.StartsWith('.') -or $old.StartsWith('-') -or $old -eq '..') {
        Write-Warning "REFUSE manifest entry '$old' is not a plain name - ignored"; continue
      }
      if ($MANAGED -contains $old) { continue }

      $target = Join-Path $dst $old
      # R5-01: Test-Path is false for a dangling reparse point. Fall back to
      # a directory-entry lookup so an abandoned link is still retired rather
      # than left behind as untracked debris.
      $exists = (Test-Path -LiteralPath $target) -or
                ((Get-Item -LiteralPath $target -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -ne $null)
      if (-not $exists) { continue }

      # Containment: the item's real parent must be this view, and the
      # retirement must affect exactly one immediate child.
      $item = Get-Item -LiteralPath $target -Force
      if ($item.Parent.FullName -ne (Get-Item -LiteralPath $dst).FullName) {
        Write-Warning "REFUSE '$old' does not resolve to an immediate child of $dst - ignored"
        $KEEP_OWNED += $old
        continue
      }

      Write-Host "retire $old from $dst (no longer in canonical)"
      if (-not $DRY) {
        # R4-02: per-view archive dir, and archival must SUCCEED first.
        # Strip the leading dot so the archive is not a hidden directory.
        $viewTag = ((Get-Item -LiteralPath $dst).Parent.Name) -replace '^\.', ''
        $adir    = Join-Path $ARCHIVE_ROOT $viewTag
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $adir | Out-Null
        $adest = Join-Path $adir $old
        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $adest) {
          Stop-Fatal "archive collision at $adest - refusing to delete" 3
        }
        try {
          Copy-Item -LiteralPath $target -Destination $adest -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction Stop
        } catch {
          Stop-Fatal "archive of '$old' failed - refusing to delete: $_" 3
        }
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $adest)) {
          Stop-Fatal "archive of '$old' not readable back - refusing to delete" 3
        }
        # R8-04: if the retired entry is itself a link, delete ONLY the link.
        # Remove-Item -Recurse on a junction can follow it into the target.
        if (Test-IsLink $target) {
          (Get-Item -LiteralPath $target -Force).Delete()
        } else {
          Remove-Item -LiteralPath $target -Recurse -Force
        }
      }
    }
  }

  foreach ($s in $MANAGED) {
    if ($DRY) { Write-Host "would sync $s -> $dst (copy)"; continue }
    $target = Join-Path $dst $s
    if (Test-IsLink $target) {
      (Get-Item -LiteralPath $target -Force).Delete()   # R8-04: the link only
    } elseif (Test-Path -LiteralPath $target) {
      Remove-Item -LiteralPath $target -Recurse -Force
    }
    Copy-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path $SRC $s) -Destination $target -Recurse -Force
  }

  if (-not $DRY) {
    Set-Content -LiteralPath $manifestPath -Value (@($MANAGED + $KEEP_OWNED) | Sort-Object -Unique)
    Write-Host "synced $($MANAGED.Count) entries -> $dst (copy); manifest written"
  }
}

if ($DRY) { Write-Host "(DRY RUN - set DRY_RUN=1 cleared to apply)" }
exit 0

```sh

# Deleting a tracked link is allowed: its new mode is 000000.
bad=$(git diff --cached --raw --no-renames --diff-filter=ACMRT \

  echo "then: git reset -q -- <path>" >&2
  exit 1
fi
exit 0

**The portable frontmatter contract** (a superset — Codex ignores keys it does not know, Claude Code ignores `metadata`):

```yaml
---
name: skill-name                       # REQUIRED. Must equal the directory name.
                                       # TitleCase is allowed (CreateSkill, Harvest).
description: >-                        # REQUIRED. <=1024 chars. Must contain BOTH:
  <what it does, one sentence>.        #   (a) a positive clause: "Use when ..." with
  Use when <literal trigger phrases>.  #       literal phrases the user would type
  Do not use when <negative>.          #   (b) a negative clause: "Do not use ..." /
                                       #       "NOT FOR ..." - Codex needs this to
                                       #       avoid over-firing
metadata:
  short-description: <one short line>  # optional, Codex-only, Claude ignores
argument-hint: "[...]"                 # optional, Claude-only, Codex ignores
allowed-tools: Read, Bash, Grep        # optional, Claude-only, Codex ignores
---
```

Claude Code triggers on literal phrases; Codex leans on the negative clause. A description with only one half fires reliably in one harness and badly in the other. **Naming is settled here (R7):** the rule is `name` equals the directory name. TitleCase is legal — `CreateSkill` and `Harvest` already ship that way and renaming them would break every cross-reference.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check every skill in the canonical repo against the portable frontmatter
contract. Exit 0 = all pass, 1 = failures, 2 = empty/missing inventory.
stdlib only (PEP 668 machine). Parses the flat YAML subset we actually use."""
import os, re, sys, glob

CANON = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/skills")
# R8-03: every key the roster actually uses today, measured with
#   grep '^[a-z-]*:' ~/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md | sort | uniq -c
# The contract may not outlaw keys Claude Code honours. `effort` and
# `user-invocable` are live Claude Code keys; `repository` and `homepage`
# are package metadata. Genuinely unknown keys are still reported.
ALLOWED = {"name", "description", "metadata", "argument-hint", "allowed-tools",
           "model", "disable-model-invocation", "license", "version", "author",
           "effort", "user-invocable", "repository", "homepage"}
POSITIVE = ("use when", "use for", "use this skill when", "invoke when")
NEGATIVE = ("do not use", "don't use", "not for", "never use")

def frontmatter(text):
    if not text.startswith("---"):
        return None
    end = text.find("\n---", 3)
    return None if end == -1 else text[4:end]

def top_keys(fm):
    return [m.group(1) for m in re.finditer(r"(?m)^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)\s*:", fm)]

def scalar(fm, key):
    """Read a flat scalar, including >- and | block styles."""
    m = re.search(rf"(?ms)^{re.escape(key)}\s*:[ \t]*(.*?)(?=^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*\s*:|\Z)", fm)
    if not m:
        return ""
    raw = m.group(1)
    raw = re.sub(r"^[>|][-+]?\s*\n", "", raw)          # strip a block indicator
    val = " ".join(l.strip() for l in raw.splitlines() if l.strip())
    return val.strip().strip('"').strip("'")

def check(path):
    name = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(path))
    problems = []
    fm = frontmatter(open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").read())
    if fm is None:
        return name, ["no YAML frontmatter"]
    keys = top_keys(fm)
    declared = scalar(fm, "name")
    if "name" not in keys:
        problems.append("missing 'name'")
    elif declared != name:
        problems.append(f"name '{declared}' != directory '{name}'")
    desc = scalar(fm, "description")
    if not desc:
        problems.append("missing 'description'")
    else:
        low = desc.lower()
        if len(desc) > 1024:
            problems.append(f"description {len(desc)} chars (>1024)")
        problems.extend(clause_problems(low))
    # R2-05: reject syntax outside the supported subset rather than
    # silently accepting it. Duplicate keys and unbalanced quotes both
    # parse "successfully" with a regex reader and mean something else
    # to a real YAML loader.
    for k in keys:
        if k not in ALLOWED:
            problems.append(f"unknown frontmatter key '{k}'")
    dupes = {k for k in keys if keys.count(k) > 1}
    for k in sorted(dupes):
        problems.append(f"duplicate frontmatter key '{k}' - unsupported")
    for key in ("name", "description"):
        raw = raw_scalar(fm, key)
        if raw and raw[:1] in ("'", '"') and not raw.endswith(raw[0]):
            problems.append(f"'{key}' has an unbalanced quote")
    return name, problems

def raw_scalar(fm, key):
    m = re.search(rf"(?m)^{re.escape(key)}\s*:[ \t]*(.*)$", fm)
    return m.group(1).strip() if m else ""

def clause_problems(low):
    """A positive phrase governed by a negative phrase does not count as a
    trigger. 'do not use when auditing' must NOT satisfy the positive check.

    R3-04: containment was the wrong test. 'do not use' spans [0,10) and
    'use when' spans [7,15) - the positive is not CONTAINED, it OVERLAPS.
    A negative span is therefore extended through any immediately following
    'when'/'for' so it governs the whole construction, and any positive match
    OVERLAPPING a negative span is discarded."""
    out = []

    # Build negative spans, extended through a trailing 'when'/'for' so that
    # 'do not use when' is one governing construction, not 'do not use' + a
    # stray 'use when' the positive check could claim.
    neg_spans = []
    for n in NEGATIVE:
        # R8-10: whole words only. A bare substring match let "not formatted"
        # count as "not for" and "because formatting" as "use for".
        for m in re.finditer(r"\b" + re.escape(n) + r"\b", low):
            start, end = m.start(), m.end()
            for word in (" when", " for"):
                w_end = end + len(word)
                if low.startswith(word, end) and (w_end == len(low) or not low[w_end].isalnum()):
                    end = w_end
                    break
            neg_spans.append((start, end))

    def overlaps_negative(i, j):
        return any(i < b and a < j for a, b in neg_spans)   # interval overlap

    pos_found = False
    for p in POSITIVE:
        for m in re.finditer(r"\b" + re.escape(p) + r"\b", low):
            if not overlaps_negative(m.start(), m.end()):
                pos_found = True
                break
        if pos_found:
            break

    if not pos_found:
        out.append("no standalone positive clause ('Use when ...') - Claude will "
                   "not trigger (a 'use when' governed by 'do not use when' does not count)")
    if not neg_spans:
        out.append("no negative clause ('Do not use ...') - Codex over-fires")
    return out

def main():
    if not os.path.isdir(CANON):
        print(f"FATAL canonical dir missing: {CANON}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    # R8-01: check only OWNED skills - real directories. A symlinked skill was
    # installed by the skills CLI or vendored; its frontmatter belongs to a
    # third party, and demanding our contract of it makes "0 failing"
    # unreachable. Ownership is structural, so no name list is kept.
    paths = [p for p in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(CANON, "*", "SKILL.md")))
             if not os.path.islink(os.path.dirname(p))]
    if not paths:
        print(f"FATAL no SKILL.md found under {CANON} - refusing to report success",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    failed = 0
    for p in paths:
        name, probs = check(p)
        if probs:
            failed += 1
            print(f"FAIL {name}")
            for x in probs:
                print(f"       - {x}")
    print(f"\nchecked {len(paths)} skills, {failed} failing, {len(paths)-failed} portable")
    return 1 if failed else 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

## The question that governs a skill's fate

Not "how often did I run it?" but **"would the current model do this fine
without the skill?"** If yes, the skill is a crutch that now limits the model.

## Delegation contract (R2-09)

A delegate is invoked **read-only**, for a **named scope**, and its receipt is
written **only** for the scope it actually covered.

1. **Read-only.** Before invoking a delegate, instruct it explicitly: report
   findings, apply nothing, write no ledger, create no files. Several delegates

   `~/.claude/projects/*/memory/` or `global-memory/`. Those are audited by

3. **A receipt covers only what was checked.** If a delegate returns findings for

CANON = f"{H}/.claude/skills"
POOL = f"{H}/.agents/skills"
CODEX = f"{H}/.codex/skills"
BUILTIN = {'exit','clear','compact','rename','color','login','logout','plugin',
'doctor','help','model','config','resume','cost','status','init','agents','mcp',
'hooks','memory','review','vim','terminal-setup','install-github-app','add-dir',
'bug','release-notes','pr-comments','ide','permissions','statusline',
'output-style','todos','export','privacy-settings','upgrade','fast','artifacts',
'tasks','loop','context','usage','rewind','sandbox','feedback','worktrees',
'skills','reload-skills','reload-plugins','bashes','keybindings','theme'}

# R8-01: ownership is structural. A real directory holding a SKILL.md is ours;
# a symlink was installed by the skills CLI or vendored. The same rule is used
# by skill-portability-check.py and both sync scripts - no name list to keep
# in step across four files.

def owned(root):
    """Names under root that are OURS: a real directory holding a SKILL.md."""
    out = set()
    for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "*")):
        b = os.path.basename(d)
        if b.startswith('.') or os.path.islink(d):
            continue
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, "SKILL.md")):
            out.add(b)
    return out

def skills_in(root):
    """Count distinct skills under root, deduped by real path (R6).
    glob traverses symlinked dirs, so a link and its target counted twice."""
    seen = set()

        s = os.path.join(d, "SKILL.md")
        if os.path.isfile(s):
            seen.add(os.path.realpath(s))
    return len(seen)

def names_in(root):
    return {os.path.basename(d) for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "*"))
            if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, "SKILL.md"))}

def usage():
    c = collections.Counter()
    for f in glob.glob(f"{H}/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl", recursive=True):
        try:
            for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"):
                if 'Skill' not in line and 'command-name' not in line:
                    continue
                for m in re.finditer(
                        r'"name"\s*:\s*"Skill"\s*,\s*"input"\s*:\s*\{[^}]*?"skill"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"', line):
                    c[m.group(1)] += 1
                for m in re.finditer(r'<command-name>/([a-zA-Z0-9:_-]+)</command-name>', line):
                    c[m.group(1)] += 1
        except Exception:
            pass
    return {k: v for k, v in c.items()
            if k.split(':')[-1] not in BUILTIN and k not in BUILTIN}

def roster_tokens():
    """Frontmatter chars / 4 - what the OWNED roster costs per session.
    Symlinked third-party skills are excluded; their cost is not ours to tune."""
    total = 0
    for p in glob.glob(f"{CANON}/*/SKILL.md"):
        if os.path.islink(os.path.dirname(p)):
            continue
        try:
            t = open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").read()
            end = t.find("\n---", 3)
            if t.startswith("---") and end != -1:
                total += len(t[4:end])
        except Exception:
            pass
    return total // 4

MANIFEST = ".generated-by-sync-to-codex"

def view_manifest(root):
    """Entries sync-to-codex.sh owns in this view. Anything else is a
    third-party install (R2-02) and is reported, never flagged as an error."""
    p = os.path.join(root, MANIFEST)
    if not os.path.isfile(p):
        return None
    return {l.strip() for l in open(p, encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()}

SUPPORT = {"_shared"}

def tracked_symlinks():
    """Mode-120000 entries in the canonical repo's index. These are the ones
    that reach Windows and break there; raw on-disk links do not, once
    gitignored. Must be 0."""
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", CANON, "ls-files", "-s"],
                             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
        if out.returncode != 0:
            return "git_error"
        return sum(1 for l in out.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("120000"))
    except Exception:
        return "git_error"

def canonical_expected():
    """What the views SHOULD carry: every canonical skill plus support dirs.
    R3-07: the view's own manifest is not evidence. An empty or stale manifest
    would otherwise report zero drift while every skill was missing."""
    want = set()
    for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(CANON, "*")):
        b = os.path.basename(d)
        if b.startswith('.'):
            continue
        if os.path.islink(d):        # R8-01: third-party link, not ours to publish
            continue
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, "SKILL.md")) or b in SUPPORT:
            want.add(b)
    return want

def view_drift(root):
    """Drift = any way a view fails to be a faithful generated copy of
    canonical. Checks membership against CANONICAL (not the manifest),
    representation for this platform, link targets, and copy freshness."""
    man = view_manifest(root)
    if man is None:
        return "no_manifest"
    want = canonical_expected()
    expect_link = (sys.platform == "darwin")
    n = 0

    # 1. Manifest must agree with canonical, in both directions.
    n += len(want - man)          # canonical skill the manifest forgot
    n += len(man - want)          # manifest claims something canonical dropped

    for name in want:
        d = os.path.join(root, name)
        src = os.path.join(CANON, name)
        if not os.path.exists(d):
            n += 1                                    # missing entirely
        elif expect_link:
            if not os.path.islink(d):
                n += 1                                # edited the view
            elif os.path.realpath(d) != os.path.realpath(src):
                n += 1                                # link points somewhere else
        else:
            if os.path.islink(d):
                n += 1                                # Windows expects a copy
            elif not _same_tree(d, src):
                n += 1                                # stale copy
    return n

def _same_tree(a, b):
    """Staleness check for copy-mode views. R4-04: sizes are not enough - a
    same-length edit to a trigger phrase, a command or a config value leaves
    size signatures identical while behaviour differs. Hash the contents, and
    treat an unreadable file as a verification FAILURE, never as a match."""
    def snap(root_):
        out = {}
        for dp, _, fs in os.walk(root_):
            for f in fs:
                p = os.path.join(dp, f)
                rel = os.path.relpath(p, root_)
                try:
                    h = hashlib.sha256()
                    with open(p, "rb") as fh:
                        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(65536), b""):
                            h.update(chunk)
                    out[rel] = h.hexdigest()
                except OSError as e:
                    # Unreadable => cannot verify => must count as drift.
                    out[rel] = f"UNREADABLE:{e.errno}"
        return out
    sa, sb = snap(a), snap(b)
    if any(v.startswith("UNREADABLE:") for v in sa.values()) or \
       any(v.startswith("UNREADABLE:") for v in sb.values()):
        return False
    return sa == sb

def third_party_in_view(root):
    """Entries present in the view but not managed by sync-to-codex.
    Informational: these are npx-installed skills other harnesses may need."""
    man = view_manifest(root)
    if man is None:
        return "no_manifest"
    n = 0
    for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "*")):
        b = os.path.basename(d)
        if b.startswith('.') or b in man:
            continue
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, "SKILL.md")):
            n += 1
    return n

def dangling_in_view(root):
    """R5-01: abandoned links left after a canonical skill was deleted.
    These are invisible to every other check - view_drift only looks at
    names canonical still has, and third_party_in_view needs a readable
    SKILL.md, which a dangling link does not provide. Uses os.listdir and
    os.path.lexists so a broken link is still seen."""
    if not os.path.isdir(root):
        return 0
    n = 0
    for b in os.listdir(root):
        if b.startswith('.'):
            continue
        p = os.path.join(root, b)
        if os.path.islink(p) and not os.path.exists(p):
            n += 1
    return n

u = usage()
canon_names = owned(CANON)          # R8-01: owned roster = real directories
out = [
    ("date", datetime.date.today().isoformat()),

**Design choice, tightened after R9.** The job runs the **metrics script only**, appends a trend row, and writes a nudge. It does **not** commit, does **not** push, and does **not** run the agentic audit. Reasons, all from R9: committing from the shared working tree publishes whatever the user had staged; a `git push` failure is easy to mask; and the 09:00 backup may run up to 240 minutes, so start-time spacing is not a race guard. - [ ] **Step 1: Write the cron wrapper**

Create `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/aios-audit-cron.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Monthly: append AIOS metrics to the trend table and nudge for a real audit.
# Deliberately does NOT commit, push, or run the agentic audit (see R9):
#  - committing from the shared tree would publish the user's staged files
#  - the agentic audit proposes deletions and needs a human reading them
set -uo pipefail

REPO="$HOME/DEV/KeystoneOS"
TREND="$REPO/docs/audits/aios-trend.md"
LOG="$HOME/.claude/scripts/logs/aios-audit.log"
LOCK="$HOME/.claude/scripts/.aios-audit.lock"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")" "$(dirname "$TREND")" "$HOME/.claude/global-memory/transcripts"

exec >>"$LOG" 2>&1
echo "=== $(date -u +%FT%TZ) aios-audit-cron ==="

# Single-instance lock. mkdir is atomic; no flock on stock macOS.
# R2-06: a kill or reboot must not wedge every future run. The lock records
# its owner PID; a lock whose owner is gone, or that is older than a day, is
# stale and gets reclaimed.
acquire_lock() {
  if mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid"
    return 0
  fi
  local owner=""
  [ -f "$LOCK/pid" ] && owner="$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)"
  if [ -n "$owner" ] && kill -0 "$owner" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "ABORT live run (pid $owner) holds $LOCK"
    return 1
  fi
  # Owner is dead, or the lock has no pid file at all.
  local age_days
  age_days="$(find "$LOCK" -maxdepth 0 -mtime +1 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
  if [ -z "$owner" ] && [ "$age_days" = "0" ]; then
    echo "ABORT lock with no owner, younger than a day - waiting one cycle"
    return 1
  fi
  echo "RECLAIM stale lock (owner '${owner:-none}' not running)"
  rm -rf "$LOCK"
  if mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "ABORT could not reclaim $LOCK"
  return 1
}

if ! acquire_lock; then
  exit 0
fi
trap 'rm -rf "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null' EXIT

if ! M="$(python3 "$REPO/scripts/aios-metrics.py" 2>&1)"; then
  echo "FAIL metrics script errored:"
  echo "$M"
  exit 1
fi
echo "$M"

get() {
  local v
  v="$(printf '%s\n' "$M" | grep "^$1=" | cut -d= -f2-)"
  if [ -z "$v" ]; then echo "MISSING"; else echo "$v"; fi
}

if [ ! -f "$TREND" ]; then
  {
    echo "# AIOS trend"
    echo
    echo "One row per monthly run. Written by scripts/aios-audit-cron.sh."
    echo "The script does not commit; the human commits during the audit."
    echo
    echo "| date | owned | third-party | pool | codex | project | never used | roster tok | portability fails | tracked links |"
    echo "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"
  } > "$TREND"
fi

# R7-04: these keys MUST match aios-metrics.py exactly. A renamed metric here
# produces MISSING, which aborts the run before any row or nudge is written -
# i.e. one rename silently kills the monthly job.
ROW="$(printf '| %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s |' \
  "$(get date)" "$(get canonical_skills)" "$(get third_party_links_in_canonical)" \
  "$(get pool_skills)" "$(get codex_skills)" \
  "$(get project_skills)" "$(get never_used)" "$(get roster_tokens_est)" \
  "$(get portability_failures)" "$(get tracked_symlinks_in_canonical)")"

if printf '%s' "$ROW" | grep -q 'MISSING'; then
  echo "FAIL a metrics key did not resolve; row not written:"
  echo "$ROW"
  exit 1
fi

# R2-06: check every required write. Without errexit, a full disk or a
# read-only path would fail silently and the job would still report success.
if ! printf '%s\n' "$ROW" >> "$TREND"; then
  echo "FAIL could not append the trend row to $TREND"
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -qF "$ROW" "$TREND"; then
  echo "FAIL trend row not readable back from $TREND"
  exit 1
fi
echo "wrote: $ROW"

NUDGE="$HOME/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log"
NUDGE_TEXT="[$(date +%F)] aios-audit due - run \"audit my AI OS\" in ~/DEV/KeystoneOS (uncommitted trend row waiting)"
if ! printf '%s\n' "$NUDGE_TEXT" >> "$NUDGE"; then
  echo "FAIL could not write the nudge to $NUDGE"
  exit 1
fi

echo "=== done ok ==="
exit 0
```

# Harness-Agnostic AIOS Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Make every skill Eric owns load identically in Claude Code, Codex, and Pi from one versioned canonical folder, and build a recurring audit that keeps the whole AIOS from rotting.

**Architecture:** `~/.claude/skills/` is the canonical home — it is already its own git repo (`erash11/claude-skills`) and is the only copy that versions and crosses to Windows. It holds **real directories only; no symlink is ever committed.** `~/.agents/skills/` (Pi, Cowork) and `~/.codex/skills/` (Codex) become **generated views**, rebuilt per machine by a hardened `sync-to-codex.sh` — symlinks on Mac, copies on Windows, never authored by hand. Every skill's frontmatter is normalized to a Codex-safe core so the same file fires in all three harnesses. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# sync-to-codex.sh -- rebuild the Codex and agent-pool VIEWS from the canonical
# repo at ~/.claude/skills.
#
# CANONICAL: ~/.claude/skills   (git repo erash11/claude-skills, real dirs only)
# VIEWS:     ~/.agents/skills   (Pi, Cowork)
#            ~/.codex/skills    (Codex)
#
# Views are GENERATED from the complete canonical manifest - every directory
# holding a SKILL.md, plus declared support directories. Never author a skill
# in a view; it will be overwritten.
#
# On macOS a view entry is a symlink; on Windows the .ps1 twin copies instead.
# A written manifest records which view entries this script owns, so an audit
# can tell a generated entry from a third-party install it must not touch.
set -euo pipefail

SRC="$HOME/.claude/skills"
SUPPORT=(_shared)                 # no SKILL.md, but views need them
MODE="${SYNC_MODE:-link}"         # link | copy
DRY="${DRY_RUN:-0}"
MANIFEST_NAME=".generated-by-sync-to-codex"

# R8-01: OWNERSHIP IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A LIST.
#
#   a real directory in ~/.claude/skills  = Eric wrote it   -> ours to publish
#   a symlink in ~/.claude/skills          = installed by the
#                                            skills CLI or vendored
#                                                            -> never ours
#
# All 19 outward links here are third-party (14 recorded in
# ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json, 4 from the vendor-review package, plus
# persistent-localhost). No hard-coded name list is kept: it was 4 names
# yesterday, is 19 today, and changes on the next `npx skills add`.

# R2-01: publish EVERY canonical skill, not a hand-kept list of seven.
# A hard-coded SHARED array is why the pool drifted and why 8 canonical
# skills were missing from it entirely.
MANAGED=()
THIRD_PARTY=()
# R9-06: glob "$SRC"/* with NO trailing slash. "$SRC"/*/ matches only links
# that RESOLVE to directories, so a dangling third-party link was silently
# left out of the exclude list and the next `git add -A` would commit it.
for d in "$SRC"/*; do
  name="$(basename "$d")"
  case "$name" in .*) continue ;; esac
  # A symlink can NEVER enter MANAGED - dangling or not. That makes the
  # original R1 danger (delete-then-copy destroying a link target)
  # structurally impossible.
  if [ -L "$d" ]; then
    THIRD_PARTY+=("$name")
    [ -e "$d" ] || echo "WARN third-party link '$name' is dangling" >&2
    continue
  fi
  if [ -d "$d" ] && [ -f "$d/SKILL.md" ]; then
    MANAGED+=("$name")
  fi
done
for s in "${SUPPORT[@]}"; do
  if [ -d "$SRC/$s" ] && [ ! -L "$SRC/$s" ]; then
    MANAGED+=("$s")
  fi
done

if [ "${#MANAGED[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "FATAL no skills found under $SRC - refusing to wipe the views." >&2
  exit 2
fi

echo "canonical manifest: ${#MANAGED[@]} entries; third-party links: ${#THIRD_PARTY[@]}"

# The ONE guard worth keeping: a name we previously OWNED and published has
# become a symlink in canonical. That means someone inverted an owned skill
# by hand, and its real content now lives outside the repo. A link that is
# NOT in the old manifest is just a fresh `npx skills add` - normal, logged.
for dst_probe in "$HOME/.agents/skills" "$HOME/.codex/skills"; do
  [ -f "$dst_probe/$MANIFEST_NAME" ] || continue
  # ${arr[@]+...} form: macOS /bin/bash is 3.2, where expanding an EMPTY
  # array under `set -u` aborts with "unbound variable".
  for name in ${THIRD_PARTY[@]+"${THIRD_PARTY[@]}"}; do
    if grep -qxF -- "$name" "$dst_probe/$MANIFEST_NAME"; then
      echo "FATAL '$name' was an owned, published skill and is now a symlink in" >&2
      echo "      canonical. Its real content has moved outside the repo." >&2
      echo "      Restore it as a real directory before syncing. No changes made." >&2
      exit 2
    fi
  done
done

# R8-02 + R9-02: keep git from ever seeing the current canonical links, so the
# daily backup's `git add -A` cannot commit an `npx skills add` link.
#
# Written to .git/info/exclude, NOT the tracked .gitignore. The set of links is
# per-machine, while .gitignore is shared through erash11/claude-skills: each
# machine's sync would rewrite the other's list, the backup would push it, and
# the Mac's links would stop being ignored - R3 again. info/exclude is never
# committed. Lines outside the marked block (e.g. /.claude/RESUME.md) are kept.
# The pre-commit hook from Task 3 is the backstop for a link installed after
# the last sync.
EXCL="$SRC/.git/info/exclude"
BEGIN="# BEGIN generated-by-sync-to-codex: third-party symlinks"
END="# END generated-by-sync-to-codex"
if [ "$DRY" = "0" ] && [ -d "$SRC/.git" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$SRC/.git/info"
  tmp="$(mktemp)"
  if [ -f "$EXCL" ]; then
    awk -v b="$BEGIN" -v e="$END" '
      $0==b {skip=1} !skip {print} $0==e {skip=0}' "$EXCL" > "$tmp"
  fi
  {
    echo "$BEGIN"
    echo "# Rewritten on every sync. Per-machine. Do not edit by hand."
    echo "# No trailing slash: that matches directories only, and git does not"
    echo "# treat a symlink as a directory - the pattern would never match."
    for name in ${THIRD_PARTY[@]+"${THIRD_PARTY[@]}"}; do echo "/$name"; done
    echo "$END"
  } >> "$tmp"
  if ! cmp -s "$tmp" "$EXCL" 2>/dev/null; then
    cp "$tmp" "$EXCL"
    echo "updated $EXCL (${#THIRD_PARTY[@]} third-party links excluded)"
  fi
  rm -f "$tmp"
fi

# R3-02: the manifest is a writable file inside a view. Never hand any line
# of it to rm without proving it is a single plain basename. A line reading
# '../../.claude/skills' would otherwise delete the canonical repository on
# the next dev-sync. Separators, dot components and empties are all refused.
valid_entry() {
  case "$1" in
    ''|.|..)            return 1 ;;
    */*|*\\*)           return 1 ;;   # any path separator
    .*)                 return 1 ;;   # hidden, incl. the manifest itself
    *\**|*\?*|*\[*|*\]*) return 1 ;;  # R4-01: glob metacharacters
    -*)                 return 1 ;;   # cannot be mistaken for an option
  esac
  return 0
}

ARCHIVE_ROOT="$HOME/.agents/skills-archive/retired-$(date +%F)"

for dst in "$HOME/.agents/skills" "$HOME/.codex/skills"; do
  mkdir -p "$dst"
  KEEP_OWNED=()          # refused entries stay tracked (R5-01)
  # Retire entries this script generated before but no longer manages, so a
  # skill deleted from canonical also disappears from the views. Entries NOT
  # in the old manifest are third-party installs and are never touched.
  if [ -f "$dst/$MANIFEST_NAME" ]; then
    while IFS= read -r old; do
      if ! valid_entry "$old"; then
        [ -n "$old" ] && echo "REFUSE manifest entry '$old' is not a plain name - ignored" >&2
        continue
      fi
      # Literal, whole-line match. grep -x alone would treat the entry as a regex.
      if printf '%s\n' "${MANAGED[@]}" | grep -qxF -- "$old"; then
        continue
      fi
      # Prove containment: the resolved parent must be the view itself.
      parent="$(cd "$dst" 2>/dev/null && cd "$(dirname "./$old")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || {
        KEEP_OWNED+=("$old"); continue
      }
      if [ "$parent" != "$(cd "$dst" && pwd)" ]; then
        echo "REFUSE '$old' resolves outside $dst - ignored" >&2
        KEEP_OWNED+=("$old")
        continue
      fi
      echo "retire $old from $dst (no longer in canonical)"
      # R5-01: use -e OR -L. When a canonical skill is deleted upstream and
      # dev-sync pulls that deletion, the generated Mac symlink goes dangling
      # and -e alone is FALSE - the link would survive while its name was
      # dropped from the manifest, leaving permanent untracked view debris
      # that the audit could not see.
      if [ "$DRY" = "0" ] && { [ -e "$dst/$old" ] || [ -L "$dst/$old" ]; }; then
        # R4-02: archival must SUCCEED before removal, and each view gets its
        # own archive subdirectory. A shared path meant the second view's
        # (possibly different) copy was deleted without being preserved,
        # and a suppressed copy failure meant an unarchived delete.
        # Strip the leading dot: an archive under '.agents/' is a hidden
        # directory a human looking for their retired skill will not see.
        view_tag="$(basename "$(dirname "$dst")" | sed 's/^\.//')"   # agents | codex
        adir="$ARCHIVE_ROOT/$view_tag"
        mkdir -p "$adir" || { echo "FATAL cannot create $adir" >&2; exit 3; }
        if [ -e "$adir/$old" ] || [ -L "$adir/$old" ]; then
          echo "FATAL archive collision at $adir/$old - refusing to delete" >&2
          exit 3
        fi
        # -P copies a symlink AS a link, so a dangling one archives fine
        # without needing its target to exist.
        if ! cp -RP "$dst/$old" "$adir/$old"; then
          echo "FATAL archive of '$old' failed - refusing to delete" >&2
          exit 3
        fi
        if [ ! -e "$adir/$old" ] && [ ! -L "$adir/$old" ]; then
          echo "FATAL archive of '$old' not readable back - refusing to delete" >&2
          exit 3
        fi
        rm -rf "$dst/$old"
      fi
    done < "$dst/$MANIFEST_NAME"
  fi

  for s in "${MANAGED[@]}"; do
    if [ "$DRY" = "1" ]; then
      echo "would sync $s -> $dst ($MODE)"
      continue
    fi
    # Safe: $SRC/$s is proven real, so removing the view cannot touch it.
    rm -rf "${dst:?}/${s:?}"
    if [ "$MODE" = "link" ]; then
      ln -s "$SRC/$s" "$dst/$s"
    else
      cp -R "$SRC/$s" "$dst/$s"
    fi
  done

  if [ "$DRY" = "0" ]; then
    # R5-01: ownership is only released when retirement actually succeeded.
    # An entry we REFUSED stays in the manifest, so it remains tracked and
    # the next run (or the audit) still sees it, instead of becoming
    # untracked debris.
    if [ "${#KEEP_OWNED[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "${MANAGED[@]}" "${KEEP_OWNED[@]}" | sort -u > "$dst/$MANIFEST_NAME"
      echo "WARN retained ownership of ${#KEEP_OWNED[@]} refused entries: ${KEEP_OWNED[*]}" >&2
    else
      printf '%s\n' "${MANAGED[@]}" > "$dst/$MANIFEST_NAME"
    fi
    echo "synced ${#MANAGED[@]} entries -> $dst ($MODE); manifest written"
  fi
done

if [ "$DRY" = "1" ]; then
  echo "(DRY RUN - set DRY_RUN=0 to apply)"
fi
exit 0

    }
  }
}

# R8-02 + R9-02: per-machine exclude list in .git/info/exclude - never the
# tracked .gitignore, which both machines share. Written only when the content
# changed, with LF endings, so a no-op sync never dirties anything.
$EXCL  = Join-Path $SRC '.git\info\exclude'
$BEGIN = '# BEGIN generated-by-sync-to-codex: third-party symlinks'
$END   = '# END generated-by-sync-to-codex'
if ((-not $DRY) -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $SRC '.git') -PathType Container)) {
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Join-Path $SRC '.git\info') | Out-Null
  $kept = @()
  if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $EXCL) {
    $skip = $false
    foreach ($line in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $EXCL)) {
      if ($line -eq $BEGIN) { $skip = $true; continue }
      if ($line -eq $END)   { $skip = $false; continue }
      if (-not $skip) { $kept += $line }
    }
  }
  $block  = @($BEGIN, '# Rewritten on every sync. Per-machine. Do not edit by hand.',
              '# No trailing slash: a trailing slash never matches a symlink.')
  $block += @($THIRD_PARTY | ForEach-Object { "/$_" })
  $block += $END
  $newText = (($kept + $block) -join "`n") + "`n"
  $oldText = if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $EXCL) { [IO.File]::ReadAllText($EXCL) } else { '' }
  if ($newText -ne $oldText) {
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($EXCL, $newText)
    Write-Host "updated $EXCL ($($THIRD_PARTY.Count) third-party links excluded)"
  }
}

foreach ($dst in @((Join-Path $HOME '.agents\skills'), (Join-Path $HOME '.codex\skills'))) {
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dst | Out-Null
  $manifestPath = Join-Path $dst $MANIFESTNAME
  $KEEP_OWNED   = @()   # R8-11: refused retirements stay tracked, as in bash

  # Retire entries no longer managed. R3-02: validate each line is a plain
  # name before it reaches Remove-Item, and archive before removing.
  if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $manifestPath) {
    # R4-01: EVERY manifest-derived filesystem call uses -LiteralPath, and
    # wildcard metacharacters are refused before any mutation. Without this a
    # manifest line of '*' passes a separator check and then expands inside
    # Remove-Item's wildcard-aware -Path, wiping third-party entries and the
    # Codex .system assets.
    foreach ($old in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $manifestPath)) {
      $old = $old.Trim()
      if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($old)) { continue }
      if ($old -match '[\\/]' -or $old -match '[\*\?\[\]]' -or
          $old.StartsWith('.') -or $old.StartsWith('-') -or $old -eq '..') {
        Write-Warning "REFUSE manifest entry '$old' is not a plain name - ignored"; continue
      }
      if ($MANAGED -contains $old) { continue }

      $target = Join-Path $dst $old
      # R5-01: Test-Path is false for a dangling reparse point. Fall back to
      # a directory-entry lookup so an abandoned link is still retired rather
      # than left behind as untracked debris.
      $exists = (Test-Path -LiteralPath $target) -or
                ((Get-Item -LiteralPath $target -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -ne $null)
      if (-not $exists) { continue }

      # Containment: the item's real parent must be this view, and the
      # retirement must affect exactly one immediate child.
      $item = Get-Item -LiteralPath $target -Force
      if ($item.Parent.FullName -ne (Get-Item -LiteralPath $dst).FullName) {
        Write-Warning "REFUSE '$old' does not resolve to an immediate child of $dst - ignored"
        $KEEP_OWNED += $old
        continue
      }

      Write-Host "retire $old from $dst (no longer in canonical)"
      if (-not $DRY) {
        # R4-02: per-view archive dir, and archival must SUCCEED first.
        # Strip the leading dot so the archive is not a hidden directory.
        $viewTag = ((Get-Item -LiteralPath $dst).Parent.Name) -replace '^\.', ''
        $adir    = Join-Path $ARCHIVE_ROOT $viewTag
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $adir | Out-Null
        $adest = Join-Path $adir $old
        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $adest) {
          Stop-Fatal "archive collision at $adest - refusing to delete" 3
        }
        try {
          Copy-Item -LiteralPath $target -Destination $adest -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction Stop
        } catch {
          Stop-Fatal "archive of '$old' failed - refusing to delete: $_" 3
        }
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $adest)) {
          Stop-Fatal "archive of '$old' not readable back - refusing to delete" 3
        }
        # R8-04: if the retired entry is itself a link, delete ONLY the link.
        # Remove-Item -Recurse on a junction can follow it into the target.
        if (Test-IsLink $target) {
          (Get-Item -LiteralPath $target -Force).Delete()
        } else {
          Remove-Item -LiteralPath $target -Recurse -Force
        }
      }
    }
  }

  foreach ($s in $MANAGED) {
    if ($DRY) { Write-Host "would sync $s -> $dst (copy)"; continue }
    $target = Join-Path $dst $s
    if (Test-IsLink $target) {
      (Get-Item -LiteralPath $target -Force).Delete()   # R8-04: the link only
    } elseif (Test-Path -LiteralPath $target) {
      Remove-Item -LiteralPath $target -Recurse -Force
    }
    Copy-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path $SRC $s) -Destination $target -Recurse -Force
  }

  if (-not $DRY) {
    Set-Content -LiteralPath $manifestPath -Value (@($MANAGED + $KEEP_OWNED) | Sort-Object -Unique)
    Write-Host "synced $($MANAGED.Count) entries -> $dst (copy); manifest written"
  }
}

if ($DRY) { Write-Host "(DRY RUN - set DRY_RUN=1 cleared to apply)" }
exit 0
```

# pre-commit: refuse to commit any NEW or CHANGED symlink (git mode 120000).
# Deleting a tracked link is allowed: its new mode is 000000.
bad=$(git diff --cached --raw --no-renames --diff-filter=ACMRT \
      | awk -F'\t' '{ split($1, m, " "); if (m[2] == "120000") print $2 }')

  echo "Fix: bash ~/.claude/skills/sync-to-codex.sh   (adds them to .git/info/exclude)" >&2
  echo "then: git reset -q -- <path>" >&2
  exit 1
fi
exit 0

**The portable frontmatter contract** (a superset — Codex ignores keys it does not know, Claude Code ignores `metadata`):

```yaml
---
name: skill-name                       # REQUIRED. Must equal the directory name.

description: >-                        # REQUIRED. <=1024 chars. Must contain BOTH:
  <what it does, one sentence>.        #   (a) a positive clause: "Use when ..." with
  Use when <literal trigger phrases>.  #       literal phrases the user would type
  Do not use when <negative>.          #   (b) a negative clause: "Do not use ..." /
                                       #       "NOT FOR ..." - Codex needs this to
                                       #       avoid over-firing
metadata:
  short-description: <one short line>  # optional, Codex-only, Claude ignores
argument-hint: "[...]"                 # optional, Claude-only, Codex ignores
allowed-tools: Read, Bash, Grep        # optional, Claude-only, Codex ignores
---

Claude Code triggers on literal phrases; Codex leans on the negative clause. A description with only one half fires reliably in one harness and badly in the other. **Naming is settled here (R7):** the rule is `name` equals the directory name. ```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check every skill in the canonical repo against the portable frontmatter
contract. Exit 0 = all pass, 1 = failures, 2 = empty/missing inventory.
stdlib only (PEP 668 machine). Parses the flat YAML subset we actually use."""
import os, re, sys, glob

CANON = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/skills")
# R8-03: every key the roster actually uses today, measured with
#   grep '^[a-z-]*:' ~/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md | sort | uniq -c
# The contract may not outlaw keys Claude Code honours. `effort` and
# `user-invocable` are live Claude Code keys; `repository` and `homepage`
# are package metadata. Genuinely unknown keys are still reported.
ALLOWED = {"name", "description", "metadata", "argument-hint", "allowed-tools",
           "model", "disable-model-invocation", "license", "version", "author",
           "effort", "user-invocable", "repository", "homepage"}
POSITIVE = ("use when", "use for", "use this skill when", "invoke when")
NEGATIVE = ("do not use", "don't use", "not for", "never use")

def frontmatter(text):
    if not text.startswith("---"):
        return None
    end = text.find("\n---", 3)
    return None if end == -1 else text[4:end]

def top_keys(fm):
    return [m.group(1) for m in re.finditer(r"(?m)^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)\s*:", fm)]

def scalar(fm, key):
    """Read a flat scalar, including >- and | block styles."""
    m = re.search(rf"(?ms)^{re.escape(key)}\s*:[ \t]*(.*?)(?=^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*\s*:|\Z)", fm)
    if not m:
        return ""
    raw = m.group(1)
    raw = re.sub(r"^[>|][-+]?\s*\n", "", raw)          # strip a block indicator
    val = " ".join(l.strip() for l in raw.splitlines() if l.strip())
    return val.strip().strip('"').strip("'")

def check(path):
    name = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(path))
    problems = []
    fm = frontmatter(open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").read())
    if fm is None:
        return name, ["no YAML frontmatter"]
    keys = top_keys(fm)
    declared = scalar(fm, "name")
    if "name" not in keys:
        problems.append("missing 'name'")
    elif declared != name:
        problems.append(f"name '{declared}' != directory '{name}'")
    desc = scalar(fm, "description")
    if not desc:
        problems.append("missing 'description'")
    else:
        low = desc.lower()
        if len(desc) > 1024:
            problems.append(f"description {len(desc)} chars (>1024)")
        problems.extend(clause_problems(low))
    # R2-05: reject syntax outside the supported subset rather than
    # silently accepting it. Duplicate keys and unbalanced quotes both
    # parse "successfully" with a regex reader and mean something else
    # to a real YAML loader.
    for k in keys:
        if k not in ALLOWED:
            problems.append(f"unknown frontmatter key '{k}'")
    dupes = {k for k in keys if keys.count(k) > 1}
    for k in sorted(dupes):
        problems.append(f"duplicate frontmatter key '{k}' - unsupported")
    for key in ("name", "description"):
        raw = raw_scalar(fm, key)
        if raw and raw[:1] in ("'", '"') and not raw.endswith(raw[0]):
            problems.append(f"'{key}' has an unbalanced quote")
    return name, problems

def raw_scalar(fm, key):
    m = re.search(rf"(?m)^{re.escape(key)}\s*:[ \t]*(.*)$", fm)
    return m.group(1).strip() if m else ""

def clause_problems(low):
    """A positive phrase governed by a negative phrase does not count as a
    trigger. 'do not use when auditing' must NOT satisfy the positive check.

    R3-04: containment was the wrong test. 'do not use' spans [0,10) and
    'use when' spans [7,15) - the positive is not CONTAINED, it OVERLAPS.
    A negative span is therefore extended through any immediately following
    'when'/'for' so it governs the whole construction, and any positive match
    OVERLAPPING a negative span is discarded."""
    out = []

    # Build negative spans, extended through a trailing 'when'/'for' so that
    # 'do not use when' is one governing construction, not 'do not use' + a
    # stray 'use when' the positive check could claim.
    neg_spans = []
    for n in NEGATIVE:
        # R8-10: whole words only. A bare substring match let "not formatted"
        # count as "not for" and "because formatting" as "use for".
        for m in re.finditer(r"\b" + re.escape(n) + r"\b", low):
            start, end = m.start(), m.end()
            for word in (" when", " for"):
                w_end = end + len(word)
                if low.startswith(word, end) and (w_end == len(low) or not low[w_end].isalnum()):
                    end = w_end
                    break
            neg_spans.append((start, end))

    def overlaps_negative(i, j):
        return any(i < b and a < j for a, b in neg_spans)   # interval overlap

    pos_found = False
    for p in POSITIVE:
        for m in re.finditer(r"\b" + re.escape(p) + r"\b", low):
            if not overlaps_negative(m.start(), m.end()):
                pos_found = True
                break
        if pos_found:
            break

    if not pos_found:
        out.append("no standalone positive clause ('Use when ...') - Claude will "
                   "not trigger (a 'use when' governed by 'do not use when' does not count)")
    if not neg_spans:
        out.append("no negative clause ('Do not use ...') - Codex over-fires")
    return out

def main():
    if not os.path.isdir(CANON):
        print(f"FATAL canonical dir missing: {CANON}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    # R8-01: check only OWNED skills - real directories. A symlinked skill was
    # installed by the skills CLI or vendored; its frontmatter belongs to a
    # third party, and demanding our contract of it makes "0 failing"
    # unreachable. Ownership is structural, so no name list is kept.
    paths = [p for p in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(CANON, "*", "SKILL.md")))
             if not os.path.islink(os.path.dirname(p))]
    if not paths:
        print(f"FATAL no SKILL.md found under {CANON} - refusing to report success",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    failed = 0
    for p in paths:
        name, probs = check(p)
        if probs:
            failed += 1
            print(f"FAIL {name}")
            for x in probs:
                print(f"       - {x}")
    print(f"\nchecked {len(paths)} skills, {failed} failing, {len(paths)-failed} portable")
    return 1 if failed else 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

## The question that governs a skill's fate

Not "how often did I run it?" but **"would the current model do this fine
without the skill?"** If yes, the skill is a crutch that now limits the model.
Delete it. Keep only skills carrying tacit knowledge the model cannot know:
force-plate thresholds, GPS conventions, Baylor reporting norms, Eric's own
routines.

Seasonal skills (`forecast-capture`, `ingest-book`) are exempt from low-use
pressure. Judge them in season.

## Delegation contract (R2-09)

A delegate is invoked **read-only**, for a **named scope**, and its receipt is
written **only** for the scope it actually covered.

1. **Read-only.** Before invoking a delegate, instruct it explicitly: report
   findings, apply nothing, write no ledger, create no files. Several delegates
   (`improve-system` among them) begin by applying previously approved proposals
   — that must be suppressed. `aios-audit` writes only its own report and the
   `Last audited` column.
2. **Scope must be verified, not assumed.** A delegate's actual coverage is what
   its body scans, not what this table wishes it scanned. `improve-system` scans
   `~/SecondBrain/` — Notes, Knowledge, Projects. It does **not** touch
   `~/.claude/projects/*/memory/` or `global-memory/`. Those are audited by
   `aios-audit` directly.
3. **A receipt covers only what was checked.** If a delegate returns findings for
   a narrower scope than its row claims, write the date **and** a scope note, or
   leave the row `unknown`. Never stamp a date because a delegate exited cleanly.

## Layout invariants the audit must assert

- `~/.claude/skills/` is canonical, is a git repo, and contains **no TRACKED symlinks**

- Entries **not** in the manifest are third-party installs (`npx skills add`).
  They are counted and reported, **never** flagged as errors and never pruned.
- Support directories (`_shared/`) have no SKILL.md and must never be pruned.

# R8-01: ownership is structural. A real directory holding a SKILL.md is ours;
# a symlink was installed by the skills CLI or vendored. The same rule is used
# by skill-portability-check.py and both sync scripts - no name list to keep
# in step across four files.

def owned(root):
    """Names under root that are OURS: a real directory holding a SKILL.md."""
    out = set()
    for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "*")):
        b = os.path.basename(d)
        if b.startswith('.') or os.path.islink(d):
            continue
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, "SKILL.md")):
            out.add(b)
    return out

def skills_in(root):
    """Count distinct skills under root, deduped by real path (R6).
    glob traverses symlinked dirs, so a link and its target counted twice."""
    seen = set()
    for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "*")):
        s = os.path.join(d, "SKILL.md")
        if os.path.isfile(s):
            seen.add(os.path.realpath(s))
    return len(seen)

def names_in(root):
    return {os.path.basename(d) for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "*"))
            if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, "SKILL.md"))}

def usage():
    c = collections.Counter()
    for f in glob.glob(f"{H}/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl", recursive=True):
        try:
            for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"):
                if 'Skill' not in line and 'command-name' not in line:
                    continue
                for m in re.finditer(
                        r'"name"\s*:\s*"Skill"\s*,\s*"input"\s*:\s*\{[^}]*?"skill"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"', line):
                    c[m.group(1)] += 1
                for m in re.finditer(r'<command-name>/([a-zA-Z0-9:_-]+)</command-name>', line):
                    c[m.group(1)] += 1
        except Exception:
            pass
    return {k: v for k, v in c.items()
            if k.split(':')[-1] not in BUILTIN and k not in BUILTIN}

def roster_tokens():
    """Frontmatter chars / 4 - what the OWNED roster costs per session.
    Symlinked third-party skills are excluded; their cost is not ours to tune."""
    total = 0
    for p in glob.glob(f"{CANON}/*/SKILL.md"):
        if os.path.islink(os.path.dirname(p)):
            continue
        try:
            t = open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").read()
            end = t.find("\n---", 3)
            if t.startswith("---") and end != -1:
                total += len(t[4:end])
        except Exception:
            pass
    return total // 4

MANIFEST = ".generated-by-sync-to-codex"

def view_manifest(root):
    """Entries sync-to-codex.sh owns in this view. Anything else is a
    third-party install (R2-02) and is reported, never flagged as an error."""
    p = os.path.join(root, MANIFEST)
    if not os.path.isfile(p):
        return None
    return {l.strip() for l in open(p, encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()}

SUPPORT = {"_shared"}

def tracked_symlinks():
    """Mode-120000 entries in the canonical repo's index. These are the ones
    that reach Windows and break there; raw on-disk links do not, once
    gitignored. Must be 0."""
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", CANON, "ls-files", "-s"],
                             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
        if out.returncode != 0:
            return "git_error"
        return sum(1 for l in out.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("120000"))
    except Exception:
        return "git_error"

def canonical_expected():
    """What the views SHOULD carry: every canonical skill plus support dirs.
    R3-07: the view's own manifest is not evidence. An empty or stale manifest
    would otherwise report zero drift while every skill was missing."""
    want = set()
    for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(CANON, "*")):
        b = os.path.basename(d)
        if b.startswith('.'):
            continue
        if os.path.islink(d):        # R8-01: third-party link, not ours to publish
            continue
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, "SKILL.md")) or b in SUPPORT:
            want.add(b)
    return want

def view_drift(root):
    """Drift = any way a view fails to be a faithful generated copy of
    canonical. Checks membership against CANONICAL (not the manifest),
    representation for this platform, link targets, and copy freshness."""
    man = view_manifest(root)
    if man is None:
        return "no_manifest"
    want = canonical_expected()
    expect_link = (sys.platform == "darwin")
    n = 0

    # 1. Manifest must agree with canonical, in both directions.
    n += len(want - man)          # canonical skill the manifest forgot
    n += len(man - want)          # manifest claims something canonical dropped

    for name in want:
        d = os.path.join(root, name)
        src = os.path.join(CANON, name)
        if not os.path.exists(d):
            n += 1                                    # missing entirely
        elif expect_link:
            if not os.path.islink(d):
                n += 1                                # edited the view
            elif os.path.realpath(d) != os.path.realpath(src):
                n += 1                                # link points somewhere else
        else:
            if os.path.islink(d):
                n += 1                                # Windows expects a copy
            elif not _same_tree(d, src):
                n += 1                                # stale copy
    return n

def _same_tree(a, b):
    """Staleness check for copy-mode views. R4-04: sizes are not enough - a
    same-length edit to a trigger phrase, a command or a config value leaves
    size signatures identical while behaviour differs. Hash the contents, and
    treat an unreadable file as a verification FAILURE, never as a match."""
    def snap(root_):
        out = {}
        for dp, _, fs in os.walk(root_):
            for f in fs:
                p = os.path.join(dp, f)
                rel = os.path.relpath(p, root_)
                try:
                    h = hashlib.sha256()
                    with open(p, "rb") as fh:
                        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(65536), b""):
                            h.update(chunk)
                    out[rel] = h.hexdigest()
                except OSError as e:
                    # Unreadable => cannot verify => must count as drift.
                    out[rel] = f"UNREADABLE:{e.errno}"
        return out
    sa, sb = snap(a), snap(b)
    if any(v.startswith("UNREADABLE:") for v in sa.values()) or \
       any(v.startswith("UNREADABLE:") for v in sb.values()):
        return False
    return sa == sb

def third_party_in_view(root):
    """Entries present in the view but not managed by sync-to-codex.
    Informational: these are npx-installed skills other harnesses may need."""
    man = view_manifest(root)
    if man is None:
        return "no_manifest"
    n = 0
    for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "*")):
        b = os.path.basename(d)
        if b.startswith('.') or b in man:
            continue
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, "SKILL.md")):
            n += 1
    return n

def dangling_in_view(root):
    """R5-01: abandoned links left after a canonical skill was deleted.
    These are invisible to every other check - view_drift only looks at
    names canonical still has, and third_party_in_view needs a readable
    SKILL.md, which a dangling link does not provide. Uses os.listdir and
    os.path.lexists so a broken link is still seen."""
    if not os.path.isdir(root):
        return 0
    n = 0
    for b in os.listdir(root):
        if b.startswith('.'):
            continue
        p = os.path.join(root, b)
        if os.path.islink(p) and not os.path.exists(p):
            n += 1
    return n

u = usage()
canon_names = owned(CANON)          # R8-01: owned roster = real directories
out = [
    ("date", datetime.date.today().isoformat()),
    ("canonical_skills", len(canon_names)),
    ("third_party_links_in_canonical",
     len([d for d in glob.glob(f"{CANON}/*") if os.path.islink(d)])),
    ("pool_entries", len(glob.glob(f"{POOL}/*"))),
    ("pool_skills", skills_in(POOL)),
    ("codex_skills", skills_in(CODEX)),
    ("project_skills", len(glob.glob(f"{H}/DEV/*/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md"))),
    # What must be zero is TRACKED symlinks. The third-party links legitimately
    # remain on disk; they are excluded per-machine and the pre-commit hook
    # refuses to commit one, so they can never reach Windows.
    ("tracked_symlinks_in_canonical", tracked_symlinks()),
    ("pool_view_drift", view_drift(POOL)),
    ("codex_view_drift", view_drift(CODEX)),
    ("pool_third_party", third_party_in_view(POOL)),
    ("codex_third_party", third_party_in_view(CODEX)),
    ("pool_dangling", dangling_in_view(POOL)),
    ("codex_dangling", dangling_in_view(CODEX)),
    ("agents", len(glob.glob(f"{H}/.claude/agents/*.md"))),
    ("hooks_claude", len(glob.glob(f"{H}/.claude/hooks/*"))),
    ("hooks_codex", len(glob.glob(f"{H}/.codex/hooks/*"))),
    ("sessions", len(glob.glob(f"{H}/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl", recursive=True))),
    ("skills_ever_used", len(u)),
    ("skills_used_3plus", len([k for k, v in u.items() if v >= 3])),
    ("skills_used_once", len([k for k, v in u.items() if v == 1])),
    ("never_used", len(canon_names - set(u))),
    ("roster_tokens_est", roster_tokens()),
]
rc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, f"{H}/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/skill-portability-check.py"],

m = re.search(r"(\d+) failing", rc.stdout)
out.append(("portability_failures", m.group(1) if m else f"error_rc{rc.returncode}"))

for k, v in out:

**Files:**
- Create: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.aiosaudit.plist`
- Create: `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/aios-audit-cron.sh`
- Modify: `~/.claude/rot.md` (cadence note)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `aios-metrics.py` from Task 6.
- Produces: a monthly trend row in `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/docs/audits/aios-trend.md`. Terminal deliverable.

**Design choice, tightened after R9.** The job runs the **metrics script only**, appends a trend row, and writes a nudge. It does **not** commit, does **not** push, and does **not** run the agentic audit. Reasons, all from R9: committing from the shared working tree publishes whatever the user had staged; a `git push` failure is easy to mask; and the 09:00 backup may run up to 240 minutes, so start-time spacing is not a race guard. The human commits the trend row during the audit. The job's only job is to make the audit impossible to forget.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the cron wrapper**

Create `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/aios-audit-cron.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Monthly: append AIOS metrics to the trend table and nudge for a real audit.
# Deliberately does NOT commit, push, or run the agentic audit (see R9):
#  - committing from the shared tree would publish the user's staged files
#  - the agentic audit proposes deletions and needs a human reading them
set -uo pipefail

REPO="$HOME/DEV/KeystoneOS"
TREND="$REPO/docs/audits/aios-trend.md"
LOG="$HOME/.claude/scripts/logs/aios-audit.log"
LOCK="$HOME/.claude/scripts/.aios-audit.lock"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")" "$(dirname "$TREND")" "$HOME/.claude/global-memory/transcripts"

exec >>"$LOG" 2>&1
echo "=== $(date -u +%FT%TZ) aios-audit-cron ==="

# Single-instance lock. mkdir is atomic; no flock on stock macOS.
# R2-06: a kill or reboot must not wedge every future run. The lock records
# its owner PID; a lock whose owner is gone, or that is older than a day, is
# stale and gets reclaimed.
acquire_lock() {
  if mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid"
    return 0
  fi
  local owner=""
  [ -f "$LOCK/pid" ] && owner="$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)"
  if [ -n "$owner" ] && kill -0 "$owner" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "ABORT live run (pid $owner) holds $LOCK"
    return 1
  fi
  # Owner is dead, or the lock has no pid file at all.
  local age_days
  age_days="$(find "$LOCK" -maxdepth 0 -mtime +1 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
  if [ -z "$owner" ] && [ "$age_days" = "0" ]; then
    echo "ABORT lock with no owner, younger than a day - waiting one cycle"
    return 1
  fi
  echo "RECLAIM stale lock (owner '${owner:-none}' not running)"
  rm -rf "$LOCK"
  if mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "ABORT could not reclaim $LOCK"
  return 1
}

if ! acquire_lock; then
  exit 0
fi
trap 'rm -rf "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null' EXIT

if ! M="$(python3 "$REPO/scripts/aios-metrics.py" 2>&1)"; then
  echo "FAIL metrics script errored:"
  echo "$M"
  exit 1
fi
echo "$M"

get() {
  local v
  v="$(printf '%s\n' "$M" | grep "^$1=" | cut -d= -f2-)"
  if [ -z "$v" ]; then echo "MISSING"; else echo "$v"; fi
}

if [ ! -f "$TREND" ]; then
  {
    echo "# AIOS trend"
    echo
    echo "One row per monthly run. Written by scripts/aios-audit-cron.sh."
    echo "The script does not commit; the human commits during the audit."
    echo
    echo "| date | owned | third-party | pool | codex | project | never used | roster tok | portability fails | tracked links |"
    echo "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"
  } > "$TREND"
fi

# R7-04: these keys MUST match aios-metrics.py exactly. A renamed metric here
# produces MISSING, which aborts the run before any row or nudge is written -
# i.e. one rename silently kills the monthly job.
ROW="$(printf '| %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s |' \
  "$(get date)" "$(get canonical_skills)" "$(get third_party_links_in_canonical)" \
  "$(get pool_skills)" "$(get codex_skills)" \
  "$(get project_skills)" "$(get never_used)" "$(get roster_tokens_est)" \
  "$(get portability_failures)" "$(get tracked_symlinks_in_canonical)")"

if printf '%s' "$ROW" | grep -q 'MISSING'; then
  echo "FAIL a metrics key did not resolve; row not written:"
  echo "$ROW"
  exit 1
fi

# R2-06: check every required write. Without errexit, a full disk or a
# read-only path would fail silently and the job would still report success.
if ! printf '%s\n' "$ROW" >> "$TREND"; then
  echo "FAIL could not append the trend row to $TREND"
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -qF "$ROW" "$TREND"; then
  echo "FAIL trend row not readable back from $TREND"
  exit 1
fi
echo "wrote: $ROW"

NUDGE="$HOME/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log"
NUDGE_TEXT="[$(date +%F)] aios-audit due - run \"audit my AI OS\" in ~/DEV/KeystoneOS (uncommitted trend row waiting)"
if ! printf '%s\n' "$NUDGE_TEXT" >> "$NUDGE"; then
  echo "FAIL could not write the nudge to $NUDGE"
  exit 1
fi

echo "=== done ok ==="
exit 0
```

findings.path: ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1 Sync-Repo (lines 62-67); plan Task 3 Step 5b and Out of Scope 'The install procedure itself (R8-02, R9-03)'
findings.evidence: The plan says that on a day a new install lands before a sync, the backup commit 'fails visibly (surfaced at session start through .errors.log); running the sync clears it.' Neither part holds. (1) Visibility: daily-backup.ps1:65 runs `git commit ... 2>&1 | Out-Null` and never checks `$LASTEXITCODE`. Line 67 logs 'committed N change(s)' regardless, and the only `$Errors.Add` calls for repos are repo-missing, repo-diverged and repo-push. A commit rejected by the hook adds nothing to .errors.log; `$ahead` stays 0, so nothing is pushed and nothing is reported. (2) Clearing: line 64's `git add -A` has already put the new link into the index. `.git/info/exclude` only affects untracked paths, and a path that is already staged stays staged. When the sync later adds the name to the exclude list, the index is not touched. Every later `git add -A` keeps the staged link, the hook refuses every commit, and the canonical repo stops backing up and stops reaching Windows, with no message. The hook's `git reset -q -- <path>` instruction goes to stderr, which Out-Null throws away. The only possible signal is indirect: once Windows pushes, the Mac becomes behind and dirty, which is reported as the misleading `repo-diverged:skills`.
findings.fix: Do both. (a) In daily-backup.ps1, check `$LASTEXITCODE` after the commit, call `$Errors.Add("repo-commit:$name")`, and log the captured output, the same way the push is already handled. (b) Make the sync actually clear the state: after computing THIRD_PARTY, run `git -C "$SRC" reset -q -- <each THIRD_PARTY name>` when DRY=0 and `.git` exists. This resets each path's index entry to HEAD: it removes a staged-but-uncommitted link and changes nothing for a link that is still tracked in HEAD before Task 4. Optionally, have Sync-Repo for the skills repo unstage any staged new mode-120000 entries before committing. Correct the Out of Scope text, and add a scratch test: stage a new link, run the sync, confirm the commit then succeeds.
